answer: Each epoch auctions a fixed grove of cedar payout slots. An identity bids a copper bond for one slot, burned if its work proof fails, and wins only by also presenting an opal: proof minted when strangers verify a distinct job finished last epoch. One job mints exactly one opal; opals cannot be copied, split, or transferred. A lone agent bids once for one opal. A fleet of n clones must outbid itself for n slots, pushing the clearing copper price up, yet still needs n distinct stranger-verified jobs for n opals. Grove revenue is fixed, so per-clone profit falls as bids rise.
